ascension-of-isaiah.name: Ascension of Isaiah
ascension-of-isaiah.note: A Christian writing of the late first or early second century AD, perhaps built on an older Jewish story, preserved complete only in Ge'ez. Chapters 1–5 tell how King Manasseh had Isaiah sawn in two; chapters 6–11 describe Isaiah's journey through the seven heavens and his vision of the Beloved's descent and return.

lives-of-the-prophets.name: Lives of the Prophets
lives-of-the-prophets.note: Short Jewish accounts of the prophets' origins, deaths and burial places, probably first century AD, preserved in Greek in Christian copies. It says Isaiah was sawn in two under Manasseh and buried near Siloam.

gospel-of-pseudo-matthew.name: Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew
gospel-of-pseudo-matthew.note: A Latin retelling of the birth and childhood of Mary and Jesus, probably from the 600s AD, drawn largely from the Protevangelium of James. Its chapter 14 places an ox and a donkey at the manger, citing Isaiah 1:3 and Habakkuk 3:2.

isaiah-pesher-4q161.name: Isaiah Pesher (4Q161)
isaiah-pesher-4q161.note: A Qumran commentary on Isaiah 10–11, copied in the late first century BC. It reads the march of 10:28–34 as the last war against the Kittim and the shoot of 11:1–5 as the Branch of David who will rule at the end of days.

sefer-ha-milhamah.name: Sefer ha-Milhamah (4Q285)
sefer-ha-milhamah.note: A Qumran fragment, probably part of a War Rule, from the late first century BC or early first century AD. It quotes Isaiah 10:34–11:1 and tells of the Branch of David, the Prince of the Congregation, and the killing of the enemy's leader.

rule-of-the-blessings.name: Rule of the Blessings (1QSb)
rule-of-the-blessings.note: Blessings for the end of days, copied on the same scroll as the Qumran Community Rule (about 100 BC). Its blessing of the Prince of the Congregation draws on Isaiah 11:2–5.

isaiah-pesher-4q164.name: Isaiah Pesher (4Q164)
isaiah-pesher-4q164.note: A small Qumran commentary on Isaiah 54:11–12, copied in the first century BC. It reads the jewels of the rebuilt city as the community: its foundation stones are the priests and the people who laid the foundation of the council of the community, and its battlements are the twelve chief priests.

songs-of-the-sage.name: Songs of the Sage (4Q510–511)
songs-of-the-sage.note: Hymns from Qumran Cave 4, from the first century BC, in which the Instructor praises God's majesty to frighten off evil spirits. They list "liliths" among the demons, the plural that the Great Isaiah Scroll has at Isaiah 34:14.

alphabet-of-ben-sira.name: Alphabet of Ben Sira
alphabet-of-ben-sira.note: A satirical Hebrew work of the early Middle Ages (probably 800s–1000s AD) with tales about Ben Sira. It contains the earliest known form of the legend that Lilith was Adam's first wife, a story not found in Isaiah 34:14.

life-of-adam-and-eve.name: Life of Adam and Eve
life-of-adam-and-eve.note: A Jewish retelling of the lives of Adam and Eve after Eden, probably from the first centuries AD, preserved in Latin (the Vita), Greek (the Apocalypse of Moses) and other versions. In the Latin, chapters 12–16 tell how the devil refused to worship the image of God in Adam and boasted that he would set his seat above the stars and be like the Most High.

apocalypse-of-elijah.name: Apocalypse of Elijah
apocalypse-of-elijah.note: A Christian apocalypse of the third or fourth century AD, perhaps reworking Jewish material, preserved in Coptic and in a Greek fragment. Origen said Paul's saying in 1 Corinthians 2:9 came from 'the Secrets of Elijah the prophet'; that writing is lost, and the surviving Coptic Apocalypse of Elijah does not contain the saying.
